Explain why trade receivables growing much faster than sales is a warning sign.

It means a larger share of sales is on credit and the money hasn’t arrived; profit is recorded but not turned into cash. The customer may be a bad payer or the sales may be to group companies, and part of the receivables may never be collected.

Risk of bad debts or sales to related parties

Header, Columns and Signs
Read the Header Before Any Number
Title: the report type and period length. Figures are cumulative from the start of the fiscal year, not just the last three months.
Not every company’s fiscal year ends in Esfand. A fiscal year ending 09/30 → “9 months to 1405/06/31” means Dey 1404 to Shahrivar 1405.
Unregistered capital above zero means a capital increase is on the way.
Industry code to find peers; issuer status: exchange, Farabourse or base market; audited or not; consolidated or separate.
Unit: “million rials”. 4,814,954 million rials ≈ 4.8 thousand billion rials ≈ 481 billion tomans. EPS is always in rials.
Saving the page keeps only the open tab; for your archive download the Excel or PDF.
Columns and Signs
The comparison is with the same period last year, not the previous quarter. Last three months = 9-month minus 6-month.
Brackets mean negative: (1,825,415) means a cost.
The sign of the “percent change” is the effect on profit: cost of sales down 41% → “41” (good for profit); administrative expenses up 46% → “(46)”.
“--” means the sign changed (loss to profit or the reverse); a percentage is meaningless.
“Restated” means last year’s figures were corrected; read its note.
Margins aren’t on the page; work them out yourself.
In the percent change column next to “selling, general and administrative expenses” it says “(46)”. Meaning?
The expense rose 46%, which hurts profit
The expense fell 46%, which helps profit
Revenue fell 46% and the expense stayed the same
The sign shows the effect on profit, not the direction of the number.
Next to cost of sales it says “41” without brackets, and the cost went from 3,088,363 to 1,825,415. Meaning?
Cost of sales fell 41%; good for profit
Cost of sales rose 41%; bad for profit and margin
Sales grew 41%
A lower cost = a positive effect on profit, no brackets.
The percent change column shows “--”. Meaning?
The sign changed (e.g. from loss to profit); a percentage is meaningless
The previous period’s data isn’t on Codal and the company hasn’t published it yet
The change was zero and the figure stayed the same

billion tomans

Funds and the 10-Minute Routine
Fund Reports Look Different
A fund has no sales or cost of sales; it has three statements: net assets, profit and loss, and changes in net assets.
Net assets also grow when new money comes in, so they aren’t a measure of return. The measure is NAV per unit.
Payable to fund pillars = fees for the manager, custodian, auditor and market maker; the investor’s real cost.
Three questions are enough: NAV-per-unit return against the index? Fees as a percent of assets? What stocks does it hold?
The 10-Minute Routine for Every Page
1. Header: issuer, period, audited, consolidated, unit, unregistered capital
2. Compare revenue growth with inflation
3. Gross and operating margins for both years
4. Separate the “other” items above and the non-operating items below
5. Effective tax rate
6. Check EPS against capital and see its operating share
7. The restatement note
8. Write three questions for the notes and the monthly report; don’t conclude before you have answers
